utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the witness will testify in closed session, he'll be cross-examined in closed session. The curtains may be drawn down. We'll not yet turn into closed session. However, I'd like to remind the Prosecution that we are still waiting for many of the translations of the Zvornik contextual exhibits, and it goes without saying that if there are no translations there, that, of course, the time limits will be extended for the Defence to oppose against any of these documents. Having said this, we'll turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Stewart, the curtains are almost up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, we're in open session? Your Honour, I'm going to proceed cautiously because the matter that I raise does relate to the evidence I just heard, but I do believe I can deal with it conscientiously in open session in a way that doesn't involve any risks for which we were in closed session. If, of course, at any point the submissions do lead us back into closed session, well, no doubt the Trial Chamber deals with that in the usual way. But I'm going to deal with it entirely anonymously and avoid anything which points in any way in open session to identification of the witness. Your Honour, earlier today - and I don't need to go into the particular matter and shouldn't in the circumstances - but Your Honour commented on my objecting to a question that came in the course of Judges' questioning. But, Your Honour, I do wish again to register an objection to one of Your Honour's questions and a line of questioning, and it is found at page 30, line 16. And I don't need, although it would be relatively harmless to read it out anyway, but I don't need to. Your Honours will see that. May I summarise it in this way: It was a question relating to the knowledge of the witness in matters outside the particular area which we were dealing with, and then the questioning went on to invite evidence from the witness in relation to other municipalities. Your Honour will recall particularly a mention -- and again, Your Honour, I apprehend it is entirely harmless for me to say this, Zvornik came up as a particular municipality. Your Honour, there are a number of points involved in this objection. One is -- one is this. One can take them in any order really because they're all there. One is merely not a procedural matter, Your Honour. It is that in the application that was made to call this witness as a witness, that we were given as an annex -- confidential annex to the motion a list of -- it's 11 - there's a little Roman numbering - a list of 11 matters that the witness could testify about. I accept the words "inter alia," which I well understand were there. Nevertheless, that is very much in the nature of a 65 ter, but at that stage really a more advanced and more specific 65 ter summary, because when a witness of this nature is being applied for as a new witness, the case has moved on and the nature of the application implies that the specification of the areas to be covered by the witness should, in fairness, be more detailed, more helpful, and more specific than is normally found in 65 ter statements. And none of those 11 items even signal exploration with this witness of that sort of area. Secondly, Your Honour, the nature of the question and the answer invited the witness straight away to go into areas of potentially remote hearsay. It was clear that the witness was not giving any firsthand evidence in relation to this matter. And, Your Honour, if this witness's evidence in relation to those matters was to be invited by questioning in that way, then one can ask rhetorically really what limits there are to the flimsiness of the evidence which can be given in relation to such matters. And, Your Honour, one contrasts it with the procedural protections and procedural hoops that one has to go through in relation to some of this evidence. We have viva voce evidence, and one can take that particular municipality. We have viva voce witnesses in relation to that municipality. In fact, we've got one or two, as it happens, by coincidence still to come in relation to the particular municipality that I mentioned. We have 92 bis procedures to protect, well, all parties and to protect the procedure, and particularly to protect the defendant, 92 bis procedures to ensure that any evidence which is not then fully given viva voce and fully tested by cross-examination is properly and fairly admissible under that rule, with notice, with an opportunity to put -- to respond, on the part of the Defence, with a coincidence, still to come in relation to the particular municipality I've mentioned. We have 92 bis procedures to protect, well, all parties and -- and to protect the procedure and particularly to protect the defendant -- 92 bis procedures to ensure that any evidence which is not, then, fully given viva voce and fully tested by cross-examination is properly and fairly admissible under that Rule, with notice, with an opportunity to put -- to respond on the part of the Defence, with a further response, then, invited from the other party, and then the Court, as has been indicated, all three members of the Court carefully read that material and make a ruling. Your Honour, that sort of questioning we have today in this surprising area for the Defence, as well, given that the indications as to the area to be covered by this witness, is so far outside the ambit of those normal protections and procedures for it to be -- and Your Honour, I mean this in the technical sense -- objectionable; hence my objection. I'm making it retrospectively but immediately, which I conceive to be the right thing to do, rather than wait. Your Honours have made it perfectly plain how much you dislike having interventions and objections made there and then in the middle of and interrupting Your Honour's questioning, which has the added drawback that it either has to be made in the presence of the witness or with the witness taking his headphones off or with the witness leaving court. So that's why I'm leaving it for this short interval and then bringing it up, Your Honour. But those are the essential points. And that whole line of questioning is open to objection on those grounds. And, Your Honour, the Defence does object to that whole line of questions and answers being included in the evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Your objection seems to touch quite clearly to basic differences in the adversarial trial structure and the non-adversarial trial structure. And one of the questions raised in this way is that if the Chamber wants to explore whether the witness has any relevant knowledge on areas on which he's not specifically called by the Prosecution, whether there would be limits on the Chamber's competence to explore those areas and where the protective mechanisms that apply between parties would similarly apply if the Chamber seeks to elicit information from a witness, it's certainly a matter which would need proper attention and reflection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I certainly endorse that, Your Honour, with respect. It's a serious -- it is a serious point, and I apprehend that Your Honour is accepting that as such, which I appreciate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is accepting, as I said, it certainly is a matter which would need proper attention and reflection. To that extent, of course, it's accepted. I think I've been clear on that. Any other issue to be raised? If not, we'll adjourn until next Monday. But I have to be cautious to say whether we're sitting in the morning or the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Monday morning, I take it Courtroom II --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed that the next hearing will take place next Monday in the afternoon, Courtroom II, and we'll adjourn until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of June, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.44 p.m.,
